content: Certainly. 1. Figueroa N and García-Román R conducted a cross-sectional study examining viral coinfections in Mexican children presenting with acute respiratory infections in emergency services. The findings were published in the Italian Journal of Pediatrics in 2015. 2. Doshi S, Silk BJ, Dutt D, Ahmed M, Cohen AL, and Taylor TH investigated household-level risk factors for influenza among young children in Dhaka, Bangladesh, through a case-control study. Their research was published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2015. 3. Firdaus G and Ahmad A explored the relationship between housing conditions and health outcomes in an urban center in India through a cross-sectional study. Their findings appeared in Indoor & Built Environment in 2013. 4. Fonseca Lima EJ da, Mello MJG, Albuquerque M de FPM de, and colleagues identified risk factors for community-acquired pneumonia in children under five years of age in Brazil during the post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era. This case-control study was published in BMC Pediatrics in 2016. 5. Forshey BM, Laguna-Torres VA, Vilcarromero V, and collaborators analyzed the epidemiology of influenza-like illness in the Amazon Basin of Peru during 2008–2009. Their study was published in Influenza & Other Respiratory Viruses in 2010. 6. Gares V, Panico L, Castagne R, Delpierre C, and Kelly-Irving M examined the influence of early social environments on Epstein-Barr virus infection using a prospective observational design within the Millennium Cohort Study. Their findings were published in Epidemiology & Infection in 2017. 7. Grant CC, Emery D, Milne T, and colleagues identified risk factors for community-acquired pneumonia in preschool-aged children. Their research was published in the Journal of Paediatrics & Child Health in 2012. 8. Hegab DS, Kato AM, Kabbash IA, and Dabish GM conducted a sociomedical environmental study on scabies among primary school children in Egypt, focusing on the Kafr El-Sheikh administrative area. Their findings were published in Clinical, Cosmetic & Investigational Dermatology in 2015. 9. Hosoglu S, Celen M, Geyik M, Akalin S, Ayaz C, and Acemoglu H identified risk factors for typhoid fever among adult patients in Diyarbakir, Turkey. Their study was published in Epidemiology & Infection in 2006. 10. Howie SRC, Schellenberg J, Chima O, Ideh RC, Ebruke BE, and Oluwalana C investigated the association between childhood pneumonia and factors such as crowding, bed-sharing, and nutrition in The Gambia through a case-control study. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis & Lung Disease in 2016. 11. Hughes H and Matsui EC explored disparities in pediatric asthma health, focusing on race, socioeconomic hardship, housing conditions, and asthma outcomes in a national survey. Their study was published in Academic Pediatrics in 2017. 12. Islam F, Sarma R, Debroy A, Kar S, and Pal R profiled acute respiratory tract infections in children from Assam, India, and published their findings in the Journal of Global Infectious Diseases in 2013. 13. Jaine R, Baker M, and Venugopal K examined the association between acute rheumatic fever and household crowding in a developed country. Their study was published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2011. 14. Jarousha AM and Afifi AA studied the epidemiology and risk factors associated with bacterial meningitis in children in the Gaza Strip. Their findings were published in the Iranian Journal of Public Health in 2014. 15. Kohen DE, Bougie E, and Guèvremont A analyzed the relationship between housing conditions and health outcomes among Inuit children. Their study was published in Health Reports in 2015. 16. Kristensen I and Olsen J identified determinants of acute respiratory infections in Soweto through a population-based birth cohort study. Their findings were published in the South African Medical Journal in 2006. 17. Krueger WS, Hilborn ED, Converse RR, and Wade TJ examined environmental risk factors associated with Helicobacter pylori seroprevalence in the United States using NHANES data. Their study was published in Epidemiology & Infection in 2015. 18. Kumar SG, Majumdar A, Kumar V, Naik BN, Selvaraj K, and Balajee K assessed the prevalence of acute respiratory infections among children under five years in urban and rural areas of Puducherry, India. Their findings were published in the Journal of Natural Science, Biology & Medicine in 2015. 19. Larson E, Ferng Y-H, Wong-McLoughlin J, and colleagues evaluated the impact of non-pharmaceutical interventions on upper respiratory infections and influenza in crowded urban households. Their study was published in Public Health Reports in 2010. 20. MacLennan J, Kafatos G, Neal K, Andrews N, Cameron JC, and Roberts R investigated the relationship between social behavior and meningococcal carriage in British teenagers. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2006. 21. Mathew J, Singhi S, Ray P, and Nilsson A presented preliminary results from the Community Acquired Pneumonia Etiology Study (CAPES), identifying predictors of bacterial community-acquired pneumonia in children. Their study was published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2014. 22. Mirabel M, Faucher T, Bacquelin R, Tafflet M, Germain A, and Robillard C conducted echocardiography screening to detect rheumatic heart disease in schoolchildren in French Pacific Islands. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Cardiology in 2015. 23. Mitra DK, Mullany LC, Harrison M, Mannan I, Shah R, and Begum N studied the incidence and risk factors of neonatal infections in a rural Bangladeshi population through a community-based prospective study. Their findings were published in the Journal of Health, Population & Nutrition in 2018. 24. Murray CJ, Vos T, Lozano R, Naghavi M, Flaxman AD, and Michaud C analyzed disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for 291 diseases and injuries across 21 regions from 1990 to 2010 as part of the Global Burden of Disease Study. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2012. 25. Norheim G, Sadarangani M, Omar O, and colleagues examined the association between smoking prevalence and meningococcal disease incidence in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and the Netherlands from 1975 to 2009. Their study was published in BMJ Open in 2014.
